subject.title: Session files should never be deleted — rename .deleted.* to .archived.*

question: Should OpenClaw replace the shipped `.deleted.*`/`.reset.*` transcript archive convention and physical purge behavior with a permanent archive model, and what migration/purge contract should existing users get?
rationale: The current behavior is source-proven, but choosing new filenames, archive directory layout, config/default behavior, and whether physical deletion remains allowed changes shipped storage and operator expectations.

options.title: Adopt durable archive contract
options.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, migrate or doctor old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and make any physical purge explicit and documented.

options.title: Keep suffixes and clarify docs
options.body: Preserve current filenames and cleanup semantics, but document that `.deleted.*` means detached until retention or disk pressure removes it.

options.title: Split into narrower trackers
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/80263 for terminology/config clarity and keep this issue for the stricter no-physical-delete durability decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt durable archive contract
recommendation.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, migrate or doctor old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and make any physical purge explicit and documented.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a user-facing core session lifecycle and compatibility decision, and steipete is the best available recent session-area routing owner from the history read.
